title: 13 Nov 2026

topics.news: CAG audits discoms first (FY21–FY26), then transmission, generation, renewables, RDSS. Private discoms are outside scope.

blocks.h: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

rows: Independent constitutional authority that audits the accounts of the Union and States; guardian of the public purse
**Art. 148** (appointment, oath, service conditions), **149** (duties and powers), **150** (form of accounts, prescribed by the President on CAG advice), **151** (audit reports)
**President**, by warrant under hand and seal
**6 years or age 65**, whichever is earlier
Same manner and grounds as a **Supreme Court judge**: President's order after an **address by both Houses** (special majority) on proved misbehaviour or incapacity

Salary and service conditions like an SC judge, set by Parliament, cannot be varied to the holder's disadvantage during term; **barred from any further office** under the Union or a State after retirement; expenses charged on the **Consolidated Fund**
**CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971**
**Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account**, government companies, corporations, bodies substantially financed by government
To the **President** (Union) / **Governor** (State), laid before **Parliament / State Legislature**; examined by the **Public Accounts Committee (PAC)**
CAG is called the "friend, philosopher and guide" of the PAC
CAG appoints the statutory auditor and conducts supplementary audit under the **Companies Act, 2013**
Does not audit purely private companies; no direct power to enforce; works through Parliament

ul: **Controller General of Accounts** (Finance Ministry): keeps accounts; audit and accounts were separated in 1976.
**Parliamentary committees:** PAC, Estimates Committee, Committee on Public Undertakings.
**Other independent constitutional offices:** Election Commission (Art. 324), UPSC (Art. 315), Finance Commission (Art. 280), Attorney General (Art. 76), National Commissions for SC/ST.
**Anti-corruption bodies:** Central Vigilance Commission (statutory), Lokpal, CBI.
**International:** INTOSAI — the global body of Supreme Audit Institutions; India's CAG is an active member.
**Foreign counterparts:** the US Government Accountability Office, the UK National Audit Office.
Discoms are state-owned distribution companies (a few are private); they supply at tariffs below cost and have high **AT&C losses**.
Earlier fixes: **UDAY (2015)**; now **RDSS (2021)**. A CAG audit found UDAY missed its goals.
**Electricity Act, 2003** is the framework; **Electricity is on the Concurrent List** (Entry 38).

prel.d: The constitutional articles on the CAG: 148 (appointment, oath, term, removal), 149 (duties and powers), 150 (form of accounts, set by the President on the CAG's advice) and 151 (audit reports go to the President or Governor and then to Parliament or the Legislature).
The Comptroller and Auditor-General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971: the law that spells out what the CAG audits and how.
Public Accounts Committee of Parliament (15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members). It examines CAG reports on how public money was spent; by convention an Opposition member chairs it.
International Organisation of Supreme Audit Institutions: the global body of national audit offices such as India's CAG.
Article 266: the main government account into which all revenue, loans and repayments flow. Money leaves it only with Parliament's approval.
Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (2015): States took over discom debt so the distribution companies could recover. CAG audits found its targets were missed.
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (2021): central money linked to performance, for cutting discom losses, smart meters and stronger networks.
Aggregate Technical and Commercial losses: the share of electricity fed into the grid that is lost on the lines or never paid for (theft, billing gaps).

qs.q: The CAG's role has moved beyond checking the legality of spending to its propriety and performance. In this light, examine the scope and limits of the CAG's powers, with reference to audits of the power sector.
qs.ref: 2024 GS2 (CAG: legality and propriety) · 2016 GS2 (Article 149 and audit of policy)

qs.q: Explain how the method of appointment and the terms of service of the CAG protect its independence. Why are audit findings often not acted upon, and how can the Public Accounts Committee make them count?
qs.ref: 2018 GS2 (CAG appointment and powers) · 2017 GS2 (role of the PAC) · 2023 GS2 (financial committees)

qs.q: Discoms keep making losses despite rescue schemes such as UDAY. Analyse the reasons and suggest reforms for the power distribution sector.

topics.news: op-ed says the 2025-26 Special Intensive Revision is a technology failure: central ERONet platform, "logical discrepancy" flags, name-matching errors, Form 6 mismatch, unpublished hearing rules.

rows: Permanent constitutional body for **elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President**; **Art. 324**
Chief Election Commissioner + other Election Commissioners, fixed by the President
**Act of 2023**: selection committee of PM, a Union Minister and the Leader of Opposition (after the Supreme Court's 2023 ruling asked for a neutral process)
**CEC** only like a Supreme Court judge (special-majority address by both Houses); other Commissioners removed on the **CEC's recommendation**
**Art. 325** (one general roll, no one excluded on religion, race, caste, sex); **Art. 326** (universal adult suffrage, age **18** after the 61st Amendment, 1988)
**Representation of the People Act, 1950** (rolls, seat allocation, qualifications to register; Section 21 revision of rolls) and **1951** (conduct of elections, disqualification, corrupt practices)
Prepare and update rolls, delimitation (via Delimitation Commission), registration and symbols for parties, model code of conduct, monitor expenditure
Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), Booth Level Officer (BLO); **Form 6** (new registration), Form 7 (objection), Form 8 (correction)
**Puttaswamy (2017)** protected privacy; Aadhaar linkage is voluntary for the roll
Court did not stay it and suggested Aadhaar, EPIC and ration card be accepted; ECI said Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship. A Supreme Court verdict upholding the SIR (May 2026) has been reported.

items.p: **Similar bodies:** State Election Commissions, Delimitation Commission, UPSC, Finance Commission (all independent bodies with security of tenure).

prel.d: Special Intensive Revision: a door-to-door re-verification of the whole electoral roll in a State, unlike the routine yearly summary revision.
Gives the Election Commission of India the superintendence, direction and control of elections and the preparation of electoral rolls.
One general electoral roll for every constituency; nobody can be left out or put on a separate roll because of religion, race, caste or sex.
Elections to the Lok Sabha and Assemblies are held on adult suffrage: every citizen aged 18 or more who is not disqualified can vote (age lowered from 21 by the 61st Amendment, 1988).
Panchayat elections are run by the State Election Commission, not the ECI (Art. 243ZA does the same for municipalities).
Representation of the People Act, 1950: who can register as a voter and how electoral rolls are prepared and revised (Section 21).
Representation of the People Act, 1951: conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications of members, corrupt practices and election disputes.
The application to be added to the electoral roll, meant for new voters.
Electoral Registration Officer: the statutory officer who finalises the roll of a constituency. Booth Level Officer: the local official who visits homes, collects forms and verifies voters.
The Election Commission's online platform for managing rolls; in the SIR it flagged 'logical discrepancies' centrally.

qs.q: Discuss the powers of the Election Commission under Article 324 and the Representation of the People Act, 1950 in revising electoral rolls. Can a mass verification drive such as the SIR be reconciled with universal adult suffrage?
qs.ref: 2026 GS2 (right to vote, revision of rolls, citizenship)

qs.q: Technology can make election management accurate, but it can also exclude genuine voters. Examine with reference to the digital platform used in the SIR.
qs.ref: 2018 GS2 (EVMs and trust in elections)

qs.q: Evaluate the role of the Election Commission in ensuring free and fair elections, and suggest reforms to protect its independence and credibility.
qs.ref: 2022 GS2 (ECI and the Model Code of Conduct) · 2017 GS2 (electoral reforms)

topics.t: LADAKH polls and the Sixth Schedule
topics.news: panchayat/municipal polls on 21 Nov, hill council polls on 4 Dec; Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance want a delay; talks on statehood and Sixth Schedule stalled; Centre floated a special model under Art. 371.

blocks.h: Fifth and Sixth Schedules, Art. 371, UTs

rows: Administration and control of **Scheduled Areas** and Scheduled Tribes in all States **except Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**; Governor's report, **Tribes Advisory Council**, power to regulate land transfer
Tribal areas of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram**; **Autonomous District Councils (ADC)** and Regional Councils

Elected members plus a few nominated by the Governor; **5-year term**; makes laws on land (not reserved forest), shifting cultivation, village administration, inheritance, marriage, social customs; courts and tax powers; Governor can dissolve
**Art. 371 to 371J** give special arrangements to Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh/Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Karnataka
**Art. 239–241**; Ladakh is a UT **without a legislature** (J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019)
**73rd/74th Amendments** (Part IX, IXA); **PESA 1996** extends panchayats to Scheduled Areas
Hill Development Councils for Leh and Kargil; now six districts with their own councils
Sixth Schedule would need a constitutional amendment; NCST recommended inclusion in 2021

items.p: **People and geography:** over 90% of Ladakh's population is Scheduled Tribe; **Balti** (Kargil), **Brokpa** (Dha-Hanu), **Changpa** (nomads, **pashmina** goats, Changthang plateau). Cold desert, high passes close in winter.
**Related bodies:** National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Art. 338A), Tribal Affairs Ministry, Governor's Tribes Advisory Council.

prel.d: Provides for the administration of tribal and Scheduled Areas: 244(1) is the Fifth Schedule, 244(2) is the Sixth Schedule.
Grants-in-aid from the Centre to States for tribal welfare, including the Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas.
Special provisions for particular States (for example Nagaland, Sikkim, Mizoram). The Centre floated a similar special arrangement for Ladakh.

Fifth: Scheduled Areas in ten States, run by the Governor with a Tribes Advisory Council. Sixth: tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, run by elected councils with real law-making power, so more autonomy.
Elected council in a Sixth Schedule area (up to 30 members, five-year term). It makes laws on land, forests other than reserved ones, village administration and customs.
Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act: gives gram sabhas in Scheduled Areas a say over land, minor forest produce and local resources.
Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council: the local councils of Leh and Kargil under a 1997 law. They now exist for each of Ladakh's six districts.
Under the J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, Ladakh became a Union Territory run by the Centre through a Lieutenant Governor, with no elected assembly.
Changpa are semi-nomadic herders of the high Changthang plateau, a Scheduled Tribe. They rear the Changthangi goats that give pashmina wool.

qs.q: Why has the demand for Sixth Schedule status and statehood for Ladakh persisted? Examine the constitutional options before the Centre.
qs.ref: 2026 GS2 (federalism and regional diversity) · 2025 GS2 (J&K Reorganisation Act)

qs.q: Compare the Fifth and Sixth Schedules. Do Autonomous District Councils protect tribal land and culture better than the Fifth Schedule arrangements?
qs.ref: 2016 GS1 (constitutional provisions for Scheduled Tribes)

qs.q: Ladakh lies between China and Pakistan. Discuss why local consent and development matter for border security.
qs.ref: 2026 GS3 (Ladakh, BADP and winning hearts and minds)

topics.news: OBC groups call a protest on 28 Nov; want a drop-down list and unique caste codes; the Centre chose an open column for all but SC/ST.

rows: Decennial; **Census Act, 1948**; Census is a **Union subject** (Seventh Schedule, Entry 69, List I); conducted by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, Home Ministry
First complete synchronous census **1881**; caste last counted in **1931**; after independence only SC/ST counted
Socio-Economic and Caste Census; caste data never released

**Art. 340** (commission to study backward classes); **Kaka Kalelkar** (1953) and **Mandal Commission** (1979) → 27% OBC reservation (1990); **Indra Sawhney (1992)** upheld it, set the **50% cap** and the **creamy layer**
**Art. 15(4), 16(4)** (special provisions), **Art. 342A** (102nd Amendment: NCBC constitutional body, President lists OBC), 105th Amendment (states can list their own OBC)
A commission under Art. 340 (Rohini) examined splitting the OBC quota

prel.d: The law under which the Census is conducted: the Union Government notifies it, citizens must answer, and the data is confidential.
The President can appoint a commission to study the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes (the Kalelkar and Mandal commissions came under it).
The President notifies the lists of Scheduled Castes (341) and Scheduled Tribes (342), State by State; only Parliament can change them.

Added by the 102nd Amendment (2018): the President notifies backward classes for the Centre's list and the National Commission for Backward Classes became constitutional. The 105th Amendment (2021) restored the States' power to make their own lists.
1979 commission that recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in central jobs; implemented in 1990.
Supreme Court upheld the 27% OBC quota, set the 50% ceiling on reservations and introduced the creamy layer exclusion.
The better-off section of OBCs, excluded from reservation through an income and status test.
Socio-Economic and Caste Census: a household survey on deprivation and caste. Its caste data was never published.
With an open column the enumerator writes whatever caste the respondent says, so spellings vary. A drop-down offers a fixed coded list, which is easier to analyse but may miss some castes.

qs.q: A caste count is argued to be necessary for targeted welfare but feared to deepen caste identities. Critically examine.
qs.ref: 2023 GS1 (caste identity: fluid and static) · 2026 GS1 (is caste disappearing in urban India)

qs.q: Trace the constitutional evolution of reservation for OBCs from Article 340 to the 102nd and 105th Amendments. How does the 50% ceiling shape new demands for quotas?
qs.ref: 2026 GS2 (evolution of women's reservation) · 2026 GS2 (NCSC and NCST powers)

qs.q: Evaluate the open-column method of recording caste against a coded list in the Census. What safeguards are needed for data quality?

topics.news: Adi community protests the proposed dam (NHPC; only at Pre-Feasibility Report stage); villages to be submerged; consent claimed only for the PFR; China's Medog dam upstream; no water treaty with China.

rows: Gravity, arch, earth/rock-fill; **storage** vs **run-of-river**; "live storage" = usable water
Over 6,000 large dams; third in the world after China and the US; **Maharashtra has the most**
**Highest operating: Tehri** · **largest reservoir: Indira Sagar** · **longest: Hirakud** · **highest under construction: Dibang** · "smallest": no official answer

**State subject** (Entry 17, List II); **inter-State river regulation is Union** (Entry 56, List I); **Art. 262** (disputes); **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956**; **River Boards Act 1956**; **Brahmaputra Board (1980)**
**Central Water Commission**, **NHPC**, **National Dam Safety Authority** under the **Dam Safety Act, 2021**
**EIA Notification 2006** (public hearing, expert appraisal committee); **Forest Conservation Act 1980**; **Forest Rights Act 2006** (gram sabha consent); **LARR Act 2013** (consent, rehabilitation)
**Inner Line Permit** (Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation 1873); **Art. 371H** (Governor's special responsibility); formerly NEFA; statehood 1987

items.p: **Geography:** Yarlung Tsangpo (Tibet) → **Siang** (enters near Gelling) → joins Dibang and Lohit → **Brahmaputra**; the "Missing Link"; Upper Siang has gorges and **Mouling National Park**; eastern Himalaya is seismically active. Arunachal is India's **hydropower frontier** (about 40% of national potential).
**People:** **Adi**; faith **Donyi-Polo**; goddess **Kine Nane**; harvest festival **Solung**. At stake: burial grounds, ancestral land.
**Agriculture:** rice (staple), maize, millets; **jhum** (shifting); valley wet rice yields more; **oranges, ginger, turmeric, banana, pineapple**.

**History of dam opposition:** **Narmada Bachao Andolan** (World Bank withdrew in 1994) · **Tehri** (Sunderlal Bahuguna, built despite protests) · **Silent Valley** (dropped) · Koel-Karo · Lower Subansiri and Dibang.
**International:** Expert Level Mechanism with China (2006); GERD (Ethiopia–Egypt–Sudan); Indus Waters Treaty (see §7).

prel.d: The Brahmaputra is called the Siang in Arunachal. The Yarlung Tsangpo enters India from Tibet near Gelling, then meets the Dibang and Lohit before becoming the Brahmaputra in Assam.
National Hydroelectric Power Corporation: the central public-sector company that builds and runs hydropower projects.
Pre-Feasibility Report: the first rough study of whether a project can be built. It is not an approval.
A storage dam holds a large reservoir for power, floods and irrigation but submerges more land. A run-of-river project uses the flow with little storage.
The usable water in a reservoir, above the unusable bottom layer (dead storage).
A major tribe of Arunachal's Siang region. They follow the Donyi-Polo faith and farm rice, millets and oranges.
Created the National Dam Safety Authority and State bodies to inspect and regulate the safety of large dams.
Recognises forest dwellers' rights over land and forest produce. The gram sabha's consent is needed before forest land is diverted.
Lets Parliament make a law to settle inter-State river disputes and bar the courts; the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956 follows from it.
Environmental Impact Assessment notification: large projects need a public hearing and expert appraisal before environmental clearance.
China's planned giant hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo just upstream of the Indian border, the strategic reason the Siang dam is being pushed.

qs.q: Large Himalayan dams promise power and flood control but face growing local resistance. Examine with reference to the Siang project and earlier anti-dam movements in India.
qs.ref: 2016 GS3 (rehabilitation of settlements) · 2024 GS3 (NGOs and EIA outcomes)

qs.q: Does tribal development in India revolve around the twin issues of displacement and rehabilitation? Discuss with reference to hydropower projects in the North-East.
qs.ref: 2025 GS1 (tribal development: displacement and rehabilitation)

qs.q: Water resources are both an asset and a source of conflict in South Asia. Discuss with reference to China's plans on the Yarlung Tsangpo and India's response.
qs.ref: 2026 GS1 (water resources in South Asia)

topics.t: INDIA–BANGLADESH: Hasina row, Ganga Water Treaty
topics.news: Hasina applied for a passport; Dhaka rejects it and wants her back via extradition; the Ganga treaty expires next month; talks stalled; ties down.

rows: India helped create Bangladesh in **1971**; **Neighbourhood First** policy
**Land Boundary Agreement (2015)** implemented by the **100th Constitution Amendment**; enclaves exchanged; **Tin Bigha corridor**
Many shared rivers; **Joint Rivers Commission (1972)**; **Ganga Water Treaty (12 Dec 1996)**, 30-year term, dry-season sharing at **Farakka**; **Teesta** deal never concluded
Barrage (1975) diverts water to the **Hooghly** to keep **Kolkata port** navigable
**Extradition Act, 1962**; extradition treaty with Bangladesh (2013); **Art. 253** (Parliament legislates to implement treaties); **Art. 51** (promote peace)
**Ganga**: Gangotri → Bhagirathi → Devprayag → plains; **Padma** in Bangladesh; **Petrapole–Benapole** land port

prel.d: 30-year India–Bangladesh treaty sharing Ganga water in the dry months at Farakka. It expires in December 2026.
Barrage on the Ganga in West Bengal (1975) that diverts water into the Hooghly to flush silt and keep Kolkata port navigable.
River rising in Sikkim and flowing through North Bengal into Bangladesh. A sharing agreement has never been signed.
India and Bangladesh swapped their enclaves (111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh, 51 Bangladeshi ones came to India) and settled the boundary.
Amended the First Schedule of the Constitution to give effect to the land boundary agreement.
Indian law on surrendering fugitives to and from India; treaties set the terms, and political offences are usually excepted.
Set up in 1972 to manage the rivers India and Bangladesh share.
The busiest land port on the India–Bangladesh border (West Bengal to Jessore).

qs.q: India–Bangladesh relations are shaped as much by domestic politics as by shared rivers. Discuss with reference to the renewal of the Ganga Water Treaty and the issue of political asylum.
qs.ref: 2022 GS2 (India's role in the Sri Lanka crisis) · 2020 GS3 (Bangladesh border)

qs.q: Water-sharing treaties are tools of both cooperation and leverage. Critically examine with reference to the Ganga and the Teesta.
qs.ref: 2026 GS1 (water: asset and source of conflict)

qs.q: Examine the significance of the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement. What challenges remain in managing the India–Bangladesh border?
qs.ref: 2020 GS3 (border security: Bangladesh, Myanmar, Pakistan)

topics.t: INDUS WATERS TREATY — Court of Arbitration
topics.news: the Court (31 Aug 2026) held the treaty remains in force and abeyance is unauthorised; India does not recognise it.

ul: **Treaty 1960**, brokered by the **World Bank**; **eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan**, with limited Indian use (run-of-river hydropower, irrigation). **Permanent Indus Commission**; dispute path: questions → differences → **Neutral Expert** or **Court of Arbitration**.
Disputes: **Kishanganga**, **Ratle**, Baglihar.
**Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (1969)**: treaties cannot be unilaterally suspended; "fundamental change of circumstances" is the usual argument.
**Geography:** Indus rises near **Mansarovar** (Tibet), flows through Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan, then Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. Pakistan's agriculture depends on the Indus system.

prel.d: Brokered by the World Bank. The three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) go to India; the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) go to Pakistan, with limited Indian use.
Bilateral body with one commissioner from each country, meant to meet, inspect and share data.
A technical expert appointed to settle 'differences' on technical questions under the treaty.
An arbitration tribunal, run through the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague, for 'disputes' under the treaty. India says it does not recognise this one.
Indian run-of-river hydropower project on a Jhelum tributary that Pakistan objected to; an arbitration decided on it in 2013.
On the western rivers India may generate hydropower with limited storage, under design rules in the treaty.

prel.k: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties 1969
prel.d: Sets the rules on how treaties are interpreted, suspended and ended. Treaties cannot be dropped at will.
India's wording for suspending its performance of the treaty after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack.

qs.q: The Indus Waters Treaty survived wars but is now under strain. Examine the legal and strategic implications of India placing it in abeyance.
qs.ref: 2026 GS1 (water in South Asia) · 2024 GS3 (China and Pakistan borders)

qs.q: Compare India's position on the Indus with China's upstream actions on the Brahmaputra. What does it mean for India's water diplomacy?
What mechanisms does the Indus Waters Treaty provide for settling disputes? Why has India questioned the competence of the Court of Arbitration?

topics.news: FTA concluded earlier in 2026; supply-chain integration, Project 75(I) submarines with TKMS built in India, green partnership, students and skilled workers, Tamil Nadu hub.

ul: **FTA vs CEPA vs PTA:** an FTA removes tariffs on most goods; a CEPA also covers services, investment and cooperation; a PTA reduces tariffs on a limited list. **WTO/GATT** is the multilateral base.

**India–EU:** relations since 1962; **Strategic Partnership 2004**; **Trade and Technology Council (2022)**; FTA talks restarted after a long gap. **CBAM** (EU carbon border tax) is a concern for Indian steel, aluminium and cement.
**Domestic bodies:** Commerce Ministry, **DGFT**, **Foreign Trade Policy**, Make in India.
**Defence:** **Strategic Partnership Model (2017)** for building submarines, fighters and helicopters with foreign partners; **P-75(I)** is the conventional submarine programme.
**Germany:** federal republic of **Länder**; part of **G4** (with India, Japan, Brazil) seeking a UN Security Council seat; **migration and mobility agreement (2022)** for skilled workers.
**Geography:** Tamil Nadu's **Chennai–Oragadam–Hosur** automotive belt, **Coimbatore** for engineering and wind components.

prel.d: FTA: tariffs removed on most goods. CEPA: also covers services, investment and cooperation. PTA: tariffs cut on a limited list only.
Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism: the EU's carbon tax on imports such as steel, aluminium, cement and fertiliser, based on their carbon content.
The India–EU Trade and Technology Council (2022): a forum for cooperation on trade, technology and security.
Directorate General of Foreign Trade under the Commerce Ministry: frames the Foreign Trade Policy and issues export-import licences.
Project 75 India: the Navy's programme to build six conventional submarines in India with a foreign partner.
Since 2017, Indian private companies team up with foreign makers to build major defence platforms such as submarines in India.
Brazil, Germany, India and Japan: they back each other's claim to permanent seats on the UN Security Council.
A 2022 India–Germany agreement that makes it easier for skilled Indians, students and trainees to study and work in Germany.

qs.q: What opportunities and challenges does an India–EU free trade agreement hold for Indian manufacturing, agriculture and services? How does the EU's carbon border tax affect it?
qs.ref: 2025 GS3 (protectionism and bilateralism)

qs.q: Technology transfer and local production are central to defence partnerships such as P-75(I). Examine how they advance self-reliance in defence.
India–Germany ties have widened from trade to skills mobility and defence. Discuss, and suggest how India can benefit.
qs.ref: 2024 GS2 (the West and India as an alternative to China)

topics.news: COP31 at Antalya; many leaders absent; finance mechanics deferred; India declined the electrification pledge. Earthshot Prize held in India.

rows: Rio Earth Summit; **Conference of Parties (COP)** meets annually; **common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR)**
Binding targets on developed (Annex I) countries; Clean Development Mechanism
Hold warming well below **2°C**, pursue **1.5°C**; **NDCs** set by each country; 5-year cycles; **Art. 6** (carbon markets), **Art. 9** (developed countries' finance)
Periodic check on progress under Paris; the first concluded at COP28 (Dubai)
**Green Climate Fund**; **Loss and Damage fund** (agreed COP27, operational after COP28); **NCQG (COP29, Baku)** of at least $300 bn a year by 2035, which **India rejected as too little, too late**
UN science body that produces assessment reports

**Net zero by 2070**; Panchamrit (COP26); 500 GW non-fossil by 2030; **LiFE**; **National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008)**; **National Green Hydrogen Mission**; **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**; **Art. 48A and 51A(g)**
**International Solar Alliance** (HQ Gurugram), **Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI)**
**Montreal Protocol (1987)**, Kigali Amendment — success model for ozone
Founded 2020 by Prince William; five themes (nature, clean air, oceans, waste-free, climate); Indian finalists: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, **Mahila Housing Trust** (linked to **SEWA**, Ahmedabad)

prel.d: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992), the parent treaty. Countries meet every year at the Conference of the Parties (COP).
1997 treaty that set binding emission cuts only for developed countries.
2015 treaty to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C, through each country's own pledges.
Nationally Determined Contribution: a country's own climate pledge, renewed every five years.
Common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities: all countries share the duty, but rich countries carry more because they emitted more.
New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance (COP29, Baku): developed countries to provide at least $300 billion a year by 2035. India called it too little and too late.
A five-yearly check of the world's progress under the Paris Agreement; the first ended at COP28.
Money for countries hit by climate harm they cannot adapt to, agreed at COP27 and made operational after COP28.
India's five pledges at COP26 (2021): 500 GW non-fossil capacity and half its energy from renewables by 2030, a one-billion-tonne emissions cut, lower carbon intensity, and net zero by 2070.
International Solar Alliance (launched by India and France in 2015, HQ Gurugram) and Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (launched by India in 2019).
1987 treaty that phased out ozone-depleting substances; the Kigali Amendment (2016) added HFCs. Often cited as a success story.

qs.q: Climate finance, not emission targets, has become the main fault line in climate negotiations. Discuss with reference to the COP29 finance goal and India's position.
qs.ref: 2025 GS3 (India's climate commitments under Paris and COP26)

qs.q: Explain the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities. How relevant is it in the Paris Agreement era?
How are initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure shaping India's climate diplomacy?
qs.ref: 2021 GS3 (Green Grid Initiative at COP26)

topics.news: AQI 'severe' after Deepavali; student protests; Section 163 BNSS orders; Yamuna dead-fish spat.

rows: **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981**; **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**; **CAQM Act, 2021** (Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR; replaced EPCA)
**Art. 21** (clean air, via M.C. Mehta cases — CNG order for Delhi buses); **Art. 48A, 51A(g)**
National AQI (2014): **Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor, Severe**
Graded Response Action Plan: stage-wise curbs as AQI worsens; CAQM invoked Stage III on 6 Nov 2026 per reports
National Clean Air Programme: city-level PM reduction targets
Vehicles, construction dust, industry, biomass burning; **stubble burning** in Punjab and Haryana adds a share in November; firecrackers on Deepavali
**Temperature inversion** and low wind speed trap pollutants; Delhi lies in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**, with the Himalaya blocking dispersal
Rice–wheat cycle leaves short gap; solutions: **Happy Seeder**, PUSA decomposer, crop diversification
**PM2.5** reaches alveoli; COPD, asthma, children and pregnant women most at risk
Rises at **Yamunotri**; worst-polluted in the Delhi stretch (Wazirabad to Okhla); **Yamuna Action Plan**; fish kills linked to low oxygen and effluents

Commission for Air Quality Management in the NCR and adjoining areas (statutory body, 2021). Its orders bind the States concerned.
Graded Response Action Plan: emergency curbs that become stricter as the AQI worsens (for example construction halts and vehicle bans).
Air Quality Index (2014) with six bands: Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor, Severe.
National Clean Air Programme: city-wise targets to cut particulate pollution.
Particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres. They go deep into the lungs and can enter the bloodstream.
A warm layer of air sits over cooler air near the ground in winter and traps pollutants close to the surface.
Farmers in Punjab and Haryana burn paddy straw to clear fields quickly before wheat sowing; the smoke adds to Delhi's November smog.
The Supreme Court reads the right to life to include a clean environment (M.C. Mehta cases).
Lets a magistrate issue prohibitory orders in an emergency; it replaced Section 144 of the old CrPC.

The State should provide primary education in the mother tongue to children of linguistic minorities.
Citizens with a distinct language, script or culture have the right to conserve it.

A mission to give PVTG habitations housing, roads, water, electricity and health services.
Recognises forest dwellers' rights, including 'habitat rights' for PVTGs.

State law restricts transfer of tribal land to non-tribals

**Shillong plateau**; **Cherrapunji/Mawsynram** among the wettest places; limestone and coal belts in the Jaintia Hills
**Lakadong turmeric** (high curcumin, Jaintia Hills), pineapple, oranges, areca nut, ginger

Specialised court set up in 2010 for environmental cases.
Hand-dug narrow pits to reach thin coal seams; unsafe and unregulated. The NGT banned it in 2014.
The central law governing mining and minerals; the Supreme Court has said it applies in Sixth Schedule hill districts too.
The hilly plateau of Meghalaya, with limestone and coal belts in the Jaintia Hills and some of the wettest places on earth (Cherrapunji, Mawsynram).
Khasi, Jaintia and Garo communities trace descent and inheritance through the mother.
Patches of forest protected by community belief; in Meghalaya they are known as Law Kyntang or Law Lyngdoh.

topics.news: India's TB mortality down 38% since 2015 (global 35%); high treatment success; catastrophic costs; TB Mukt Bharat screening.

**RNTCP → National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)**; **Ni-kshay** portal; **Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana** (monthly nutrition support); **Ni-kshay Mitra** (community support)
India aimed for elimination by **2025** (missed); now aims for 2030; **WHO End TB Strategy**, **SDG 3.3**

Online portal that tracks every notified TB patient from diagnosis to treatment outcome.
Monthly cash support to TB patients for nutrition during treatment.
Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course: a health worker or volunteer watches the patient take each dose.
Multidrug-resistant TB: the bacteria resist the two main first-line drugs, isoniazid and rifampicin.
A six-month all-oral regimen of four drugs (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid, moxifloxacin) for drug-resistant TB.
WHO's plan to end the epidemic by 2030, with deaths cut by 90% and new cases by 80% compared with 2015.
When a family's TB-related spending (medicines, travel, lost wages) exceeds 20% of its yearly income.
The UN goal target to end the TB epidemic, along with AIDS and malaria, by 2030.

Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene: the rubber-like binder that also serves as fuel in solid rocket motors.
Solid motors are simple and strong but cannot be throttled or shut down; liquid engines are controllable but more complex.
A near-polar orbit in which the satellite crosses each place at the same local time, ideal for imaging.
NewSpace India Limited: ISRO's commercial arm that markets launches and services.
The agency (2020) that authorises and promotes private-sector space activity in India.
India's main launch site (Satish Dhawan Space Centre) in Andhra Pradesh, on the east coast and close to the equator.
ISRO's heavier launcher, used for Chandrayaan-3 and planned for Gaganyaan; it shares some quality processes with the PSLV.

Reading all the DNA in a sample to find which microbes and resistance genes are present.
Doctors' joint declaration that gave India its first roadmap against AMR.

Held every year from 18 to 24 November.
